sources.quote: JONG PONG JU a/k/a ‘Bryan Cho,’ and CHANG NAM IL a/k/a ‘Bong Chee Shen,’ a/k/a ‘Peter Xiao,’ were citizens of North Korea

notes: Allegation in an indictment, not an adjudicated finding.

value.context: source-reported collective travel and co-located work allegation

sources.quote: The defendants, KIM KWANG JIN, KANG TAE BOK, JONG PONG JU, and CHANG NAM IL, and others unknown to the Grand Jury, traveled to locations outside of North Korea, including the United Arab Emirates, using North Korean travel documents, and lived and worked as a co-located team.
The defendants are believed to have traveled to the United Arab Emirates in 2019 on North Korean travel documents and worked there together as a co-located team.

notes: The year comes from secondary reporting about the charged group. This is not an independently verified individual itinerary, residence, present location, or adjudicated fact.

value.employer_description: virtual token development company located in Serbia

sources.quote: Since at least in or about May 2021 and continuing until in or about February 2022, defendant JONG PONG JU, using the alias ‘Bryan Cho,’ was employed by Company-2 to provide IT services.

notes: Employer remains unnamed in the filing.

sources.quote: In or about October 2021, via Telegram, defendant JONG PONG JU, using the Telegram account for the ‘Bryan Cho’ alias, recommended that the founder of Company-2 hire ‘Peter Xiao’ as a developer.

notes: The official filing does not publish a Telegram username. Do not equate this account with [@]atroobj solely because both are reported in connection with Bryan Cho.

sources.quote: In truth, ‘Peter Xiao’ was actually defendant CHANG NAM IL, which defendant JONG PONG JU knew at the time he recommended ‘Peter Xiao’ to Company-2.

notes: The exact day in October is not stated.

sources.quote: On or about February 11, 2022, defendant JONG PONG JU, using access granted to him by Company-2, fraudulently obtained virtual currency tokens valued at approximately 60 Ether (worth approximately $175,680 at the time of the theft) from Company-2

notes: Allegation in an indictment; the victim company is intentionally unnamed.

sources.quote: On or about February 13, 2022, defendant JONG PONG JU sent virtual currency totaling approximately 60 Ether that was fraudulently obtained from Company-2 to Tornado Cash for mixing.

notes: Allegation in an indictment.

sources.quote: Today, the Northern District of Georgia unsealed a five-count wire fraud and money laundering indictment charging four North Korean nationals, Kim Kwang Jin (김관진), Kang Tae Bok (강태복), Jong Pong Ju (정봉주) and Chang Nam Il (창남일)

A five-count indictment unsealed Monday in the Northern District of Georgia names Kim Kwang Jin, Kang Tae Bok, Jong Pong Ju, and Chang Nam Il as defendants in the case, accusing them of wire fraud and money laundering.

notes: Counts involving Jong Pong Ju are alleged, and no conviction was found in the bounded review. The filed unsealing order corrects the prior profile's erroneous 1:25-cr-00232 docket value.
